body:
Chunk `2026-11-03-stdio-sidecar-retired`, taken up from the working entry `chk-jcoonzji` (Epoch 1 — Foundation:
base CI, the capability record, a console engine with its door, its gates), version andromeda-pulse-0.4.0. The
first chunk of this project taken up on the records store: the masters are read through `rec.py`, whole.

The stdio MCP sidecar leaves the product. Since `2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door` a stdio agent reaches the
door's nine tools through `andromeda-pulse-engine door`, so the sidecar's process, its double gate, what the engine
does only for it, the window's side of it and its CI job are removed, and the tests that spawned the sidecar read
through the door instead. When the chunk lands the engine has ONE way in besides telemetry — the door — and the
masters stop saying "two ways in until Stdio sidecar retired lands". Capability named by the entry: P-092.

body:
Each block is folded as a hypothesis: every named file, test, pin and master site is re-verified at P3 against the
tree and the store before it shapes the plan.

1. **CARRY `cry-d7x3pwjm` — what the cut of `2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process` left here** (the operator's
   answer at that chunk's P4, the pc overseer, 2026-10-10; record: that chunk's plan, Implementation notes):
   - the sidecar process — the `andromeda-pulse-mcp` binary and its `[[bin]]`, `feature_gate.rs`, `tracing_setup.rs`,
     the feature `mcp-server`, the `rmcp` dependency with its `deny.toml` entries, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED`, the
     crate's two subprocess tests, and the four `pulse-app` tests that spawn the binary, rewritten to read through the
     door;
   - what the engine does for it — `publish_workspace_key_for_sidecar` and `run/workspace-key`, whose only reader is
     the sidecar;
   - the window's side — `mcp_router.rs` and its test, the five wiring sites of `main.rs`, the tray item, the three
     `mcp.*` procedure pins with the bindings, `Settings.mcp_server_enabled` and the ready check of the same name, the
     Settings switch, the Send to agent button and its hook, the a11y spec and helpers;
   - in the workflow — the `mcp-test` job, and the feature on the boot job's release build with its pin.

2. **CARRY `cry-bo6jvirw`** — `cargo xtask smoke:external-resolve` is NOT this entry's: `Scenario legs driven against
   the console engine` owns moving its write to the door, in that entry's own words. Boundary of this chunk.

3. **CARRY `cry-oqvnrqx7` — what the door still says in the sidecar's voice** (found at
   `2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process`, its report, Found and not owned 1 to 3):
   - the `initialize` answer names the server `andromeda-pulse-mcp`;
   - the tool descriptions speak of "the in-memory buffer" and of "the main app's in-memory registry" learning of a
     resolve "on next launch", where the engine's reconcile step does it within one persist cycle;
   - the tools' argument structs read past an undeclared member (no `deny_unknown_fields`; the manifest's
     `additionalProperties: false` unenforced on the sidecar) and the door's own check is the only refusal —
     security-plan §Input Validation names this entry owner of that gap, with no fix built before it, and **one of the
     two forms is chosen here** (the operator's word at that chunk's Phase 2 halt, the pc overseer, 2026-10-11).

4. **CARRY `cry-f7vcog76` — the capability record's P-039** names two webview proofs of the Send to agent button
   (`pulse-app/ui/src/report/use-mcp-delivery.test.ts`, `SendToAgentButton.test.tsx`) that leave here: a removal that
   deletes a file a claimed entry names re-points that scenario in the same chunk, or `cargo xtask
   verify:capability-matrix` reads red. P-036 and P-039 also name `pulse-app/tests/e2e_p3_mcp_incident_tools.rs`, an
   in-process test of the dispatcher that stays valid while the tools crate stays.

5. **CARRY `cry-hcr5ygl7` — master text this entry settles:** test-plan §1's three sidecar pending rows
   (`workspace-key-cross-process-coverage`, `mcp-incident-read-back-cross-process-coverage`, and the security-vector
   row on MCP response body redaction) and §6 scenario P3's residual, each still true of the sidecar and none re-read
   through the door; the sentences that say the engine has two ways in until this entry lands (architecture [MCP
   Server Surface], security-plan's door vector and `rules/security.md`); and the "MCP server status change"
   notification that design-system and layout-templates name, never built (no emitter), a wording correction and not
   a removal.

6. **CARRY `cry-pvu45l6n` — the stdio way this entry waited on exists** since `2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door`
   (`andromeda-pulse-engine door`, one connection per request; architecture §Standard Contracts → Engine door, Stdio),
   and that chunk's wrap wrote "until Stdio sidecar retired lands" / "the sidecar stays the other stdio carrier" into
   architecture §Occupied Resources → Engine door surface, security-plan's MCP stdio vector and the
   stdio-is-no-longer-the-sidecar's-alone clauses of four masters; this entry settles them.

The stdio sidecar `andromeda-pulse-mcp` leaves, and with it everything that exists only for it: the binary and its
`[[bin]]`, the cargo feature `mcp-server` and the `rmcp` dependency, the runtime switch `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED`
(the double gate goes whole), the sidecar's own log sink, the `dispatch_tool` wrapper and the `mcp.*` records it alone
emits, the engine's publish of `run/workspace-key` (the sidecar its only product reader), the window app's MCP side
(the `mcp.*` router and procedures, the tray toggle, `Settings.mcp_server_enabled` and the ready check of that name,
the Settings switch, the Send to agent button and its hook) and the `mcp-test` CI job. Afterwards the engine has one
way in besides telemetry: the console engine's door, over its socket or its stdio relay (per architecture §Standard
Contracts → Engine door; security-plan §Threat Model Summary → Attack surface, the door's vector).

The `mcp-server` crate stays as the tools library the door serves (`call_tool`, the nine tools, `jsonrpc.rs`; per
architecture §Established Decisions [MCP Server Surface]). The four `pulse-app` tests that spawned the sidecar are
rewritten to read through the door. The door itself does not change: its admission, bounds, codes, socket and records
stay as they are. On the operator's P4 answers (`inputs#I2`, the overseer as the founder's delegate, PROVISIONAL):
the door's `declared_only` check stays the one refusal of an undeclared argument member, proved for all nine tools by
a committed test, and the `initialize` answer keeps `serverInfo.name = "andromeda-pulse-mcp"`. The one tool text
corrected is `mark_incident_resolved`'s description, which still speaks of the sidecar's "next launch".

The masters' sidecar sentences (two ways in, the double gate, the stdio carrier, the sidecar's sink and records, the
three product binaries, the never-built "MCP server status change" notification, test-plan §1's three sidecar
pending rows and §6 P3's residual) are the wrap's, listed under Implementation notes.

1. **The sidecar process leaves.** Delete `crates/mcp-server/src/bin/andromeda-pulse-mcp.rs`,
   `crates/mcp-server/src/feature_gate.rs`, `crates/mcp-server/src/tracing_setup.rs`,
   `crates/mcp-server/tests/sidecar_subprocess.rs` and `crates/mcp-server/tests/incident_events_subprocess.rs`. In
   `crates/mcp-server/src/lib.rs` remove the `feature_gate` and `tracing_setup` modules. In
   `crates/mcp-server/Cargo.toml` remove the `[[bin]]` table, the `[features]` table's `mcp-server` feature and the
   `rmcp` dependency, and remove each of `tracing-subscriber`, `tracing-appender`, `tracing-error`, `workspace-detector`
   and `chrono` that no remaining file of the crate names (`grep -rn '{crate_ident}' crates/mcp-server/src crates/mcp-server/tests`
   reads 0 hits; `chrono` stays — `tools.rs:604` and `:775` use it).

2. **The sidecar-only error variants leave.** In `crates/mcp-server/src/contract.rs` remove `FeatureNotEnabled`,
   `EnvVarDisabled`, `RmcpInit`, `Io` and `TracingInit` with their tests (research: no kept file raises them);
   `JsonRpcFraming`, `ToolDispatchFailed` and `ToolArgsInvalid` stay. In `crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs` remove the
   five matching arms of `impl From<McpServerError> for AppError` (:774-805) and the tests that construct a removed
   variant (:1473-1490, :1833-1850); the three kept arms and their tests stay.

3. **`dispatch_tool` and its records leave.** In `crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs` remove `dispatch_tool` and the three
   records only it writes (`mcp.tools.call.response`, `metric.mcp.tool_call_duration_ms`, `mcp.tools.call.error`;
   :198-230). Its unit tests in the same file (:801-1112) call `call_tool` instead and assert the same answers. Correct
   the doc comments that name the sidecar as the caller (:67-71, :431, :526) to name the door. `call_tool`'s signature
   and behaviour do not change (`dispatch_tool @ andromeda-pulse-mcp.rs:12/273` is its only product caller, research
   §Graph impact).

4. **The resolve description.** In `crates/mcp-server/src/jsonrpc.rs:222` replace `mark_incident_resolved`'s
   description with: "Mark an incident resolved in the persistent corpus by id. The running engine drops it from its
   active set within one persist cycle." Correct the comment at :119 ("the rmcp sidecar") to the tool list the door
   serves. `serverInfo.name` (:109) and the three query tools' descriptions stay as they are (scope: the in-memory
   buffer wording is true of the engine at HEAD).

5. **The manifests and the lockfile.** Remove the workspace `rmcp` entry and its comment block from `Cargo.toml`
   (:107-117). Remove the `mcp-server` feature from `pulse-app/Cargo.toml` (:87); the plain
   `[dependencies.mcp-server-crate]` stays. Let the next cargo build rewrite `Cargo.lock` (no `cargo update` of
   anything else). Then run `cargo deny check bans`: remove from `deny.toml [bans] skip` every entry it reports as an
   unnecessary skip (the `darling` / `darling_core` / `darling_macro` / `schemars` / `schemars_derive` group of
   :217-227 is the candidate set), and correct the provenance comments that name `rmcp` as a holder (:40-60) to
   the holders that remain. `multiple-versions = "deny"` and the `tonic` canary stay untouched (security-plan
   §Dependency Security).

6. **The window app's MCP side.** Delete `pulse-app/src/mcp_router.rs` and `pulse-app/tests/unit_mcp_router.rs`;
   remove `pub mod mcp_router` from `pulse-app/src/lib.rs` (:27-28). In `pulse-app/src/main.rs` remove the

webview gates run (this chunk writes under `pulse-app/ui/**`), and so do `cargo deny` and `cargo audit` (the manifests
and the lockfile change). This chunk changes the procedure set, so the bindings close is the procedure-changing form:
regen after the workspace run, two content probes, the bindings staged with the pin, `check:staged-artifacts`, then
`capability-drift` last; the regen runs before the `ui/dist` and release builds. With the feature gone the default
build is the full shape, so the regen carries no feature. Lean checks per `inputs#I1`: the gates this plan requires,
each run once; no repeat loop. No headful self-verify is listed: `cargo xtask self-verify` drives WebView2 through
`msedgedriver` on a Windows host, and this Linux host has none; the window smoke and the a11y suite stand in for the
UI half.

`cargo xtask test:a11y` is not a local entry: at P5 it read red on the untouched tree for a host reason
(`browserType.launch: Executable doesn't exist at ~/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium_headless_shell-1217/…`, the
Playwright headless shell is not installed on this host). Lean checks per `inputs#I1`: no browser is installed for
it; the CI `a11y` job runs the same command (`cargo xtask test:a11y`, with its regression detector and its two uploads)
and is read by name in the CI read. Locally the suite's config-named `--list` entry stands guard against a list-time
import failure.

`cargo audit` read red at P5 on the untouched tree: 42 vulnerabilities (62 distinct ids with the allowed warnings),
advisories dated up to 2026-10-29 against crates this chunk does not touch (wasmtime 48.0.5, rustls 0.23.45,
quinn-proto 0.11.15, rustls-webpki, webpki-roots, webpki-root-certs, the zstd family, zip 4.6.1, pulldown-cmark
0.13.3, tokio 1.52.1, zbus_names, zvariant, event-listener). It is external decay (playbook, External decay: routine),
and on the operator's P5 answer (`inputs#I3`, the overseer as the founder's delegate, PROVISIONAL) this chunk goes on as
a removal: the `cargo audit` entry and the CI read are report-only, the report carries the id set, and the wrap mints
the owner entry «Advisories since 2026-10-12 closed» directly after this one. No finding is ignore-listed
(`rules/security.md`: a finding with a stated safe upgrade is never ignore-listed). The CI verdict therefore reads
green on every check but `supply-chain`, whose red is that owned decay.

title: The agent's door opens onto the real data, from the engine's first step

record.title: The agent's door opens onto the real data, from the engine's first step
record.requirement: the door lives inside the engine's process and replaces the stdio sidecar as soon as the console engine exists, ahead of the removals the sidecar is built on (the credential store, the resolver, the incident it parses, the model's renderer, the workspace key), so that those chunks change the door, which stays, and never the sidecar, which goes; every reading from outside the process — the engine's own end-to-end gate, the external harness at each theme — goes through the door; an agent on the developer's machine reaches the engine's tools and reads the telemetry the engine holds, filtered by service, time range, trace and text, with aggregates; it reaches one incident whole, with its evidence, and the incidents like it from the past; it can ask for the curated snapshot — a narrow, budgeted view of recent telemetry made for a large model — which is that code's consumer from now on; the same door serves the test harness and the status widget
record.observed_gap: the MCP sidecar's four telemetry tools read their own empty in-memory database and accept only a time window and a limit; the curated snapshot and the curation crates (about 3200 lines) have the window's toast and that empty database as their only outlets. The sidecar is a second process built on what this version removes: it opens the corpus through the desktop's credential store (`crates/mcp-server/src/bin/andromeda-pulse-mcp.rs:6`), reads the published workspace key (`:78`), and renders an incident by parsing the model's answer with the model's renderer (`crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs:25-28`, `:380`). Until a door exists it is the only way anything outside the process reads a finding.

- **[Corpus Write Arbitration — which of two writers to the same incident row wins] Monotonic last-writer guard at the `CorpusWriter` choke point**: incident status writes are arbitrated by a bound `AND updated_unix_nano <= ?2` predicate appended to the existing `incidents` UPDATE, with a second bound `SELECT 1 FROM incidents WHERE id = ?1` classifying the zero-row result. `CorpusWriter::update_incident_status` and `IncidentPersistence::update_incident_status` therefore return `Result<IncidentWriteOutcome, _>` (`Applied` | `DeclinedStale`): a write whose payload is OLDER than the stored row is **DECLINED, not failed** — losing to a fresher writer is an expected outcome, and encoding it as an `Error` would make "log it as a failure" the default at every call site. `Error::QueryFailed` continues to mean the row does not exist. The predicate works because every registry mutator bumps `updated_at_unix_nano` to `now` (`mark_resolved` / `mark_read` / `attach_resolution_summary` / `attach_interpretation_summary`), so a stale snapshot necessarily carries a smaller value. **Placement is the corpus layer, not the `triage` trait**, because it is the ONLY choke point all SEVEN production writers traverse: six share `IncidentPersistence` (the persist cycle, the auto-resolve observer, `incidents.acknowledge`, `incidents.mark_resolved`, and both `inference_runtime` L4 writers) while the seventh — the `crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs` incident-resolve write (`dispatch_mark_incident_resolved` → `update_incident_status`) — calls `CorpusWriter` directly and bypasses that trait entirely. Its one carrier is the console engine's door, in the engine's own process, over the engine's own `Arc<dyn CorpusWriter>`, refused with `-32001` before the dispatcher is called unless the write switch `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DOOR_RESOLVE` reads on — so the seventh writer traverses this choke point, and the guard, its existence probe and `Applied` / `DeclinedStale` are unchanged (`the_door_resolves_an_incident_and_says_it_was_a_write`, `pulse-app/tests/integration_engine_boot.rs`, reads the row `resolved` through the engine's own `CorpusWriter`; PROVISIONAL — §Occupied Resources → Network ports, the door). The placement costs no new crate edge (`mcp-server → corpus` and `pulse-app → corpus` already exist) and no DDL. **REJECTED — a status-only predicate** (`status != 'resolved'`): disproved by measurement, since `attach_resolution_summary` REQUIRES `status == Resolved` and is the documented final write, so such a guard would break it. **REJECTED — delta-persistence** (persist only changed rows): larger, needs new dirty-tracking state with crash-loss semantics, and does nothing for the cross-process path, which is not a snapshot problem. `triage::contract::IncidentWriteOutcome` is a deliberate PARALLEL type rather than a re-export — `triage` sits below `corpus` in the dependency DAG, so the `pulse-app` adapter maps between the two. **Residual CLOSED 2026-08-29** (chunk `2026-08-29-app-registry-reconciliation`): this entry previously recorded an accepted residual — the guard made the CORPUS correct but not the app, so after an external MCP resolve the running app showed the incident active until restart and its persist cycle declined that row every cycle. That is no longer true. The 60 s incident persist cycle now RECONCILES first: it reads the durable active-incident **ids** for the workspace through `triage::contract::DurableActiveIncidents::active_incident_ids` (a narrow read port declared in `triage`, implemented at the `pulse-app` binary boundary over the SAME `Arc<dyn CorpusWriter>` the write path uses, so no new crate edge and no payload decoded in `triage`), resolves any registry row absent from that set via the existing `IncidentRegistry::mark_resolved` transition, and only then runs its write loop — so the row it just reconciled is never re-offered. A durable-read `Err` reconciles NOTHING (treating it as an empty set would match every registry row and resolve the whole active list) and warns on `triage.incident.persist.error` with `persist_kind = "incident_reconcile"`; the outcome is counted once per cycle as `reconciled_count` on `triage.incident.persist`. `load_active_incidents` remains a boot-only caller, and the monotonic predicate, its existence probe and the `Applied` / `DeclinedStale` semantics above are unchanged. Measured live: a real `andromeda-pulse-mcp` subprocess resolved a row and the running app dropped it within two persist cycles with NO restart (`reconciled_count` 1 / `declined_count` 0, against 0 / 2 under a mutation with reconciliation removed). The reconciler deliberately emits no `IncidentLifecycleEvent`: `pulse://stream/incidents` has producers but no consumer, so a send would be dead plumbing — the webview learns of the change through its existing ~1 s `incidents.list_active` poll.

- **Endpoint naming**: OTLP endpoints are spec-fixed (`/v1/traces`, `/v1/metrics`, `/v1/logs`). Tauri IPC procedures use one of two authorized shapes: (a) top-level bare `snake_case` verbs for the cross-cutting envelope (`app_info`, `health`, `ready`, `get_settings`, `update_settings`); (b) `<router>.<verb>` dotted namespaces for per-crate routers (e.g., `traces.query`, `snapshot.generate`, `plugins.list`, `workspace.detect`). Both segments are `snake_case`. Occupied Resources is the canonical procedure list; the Convention defines the shape, not the enumeration.

- **Workspace API style — internal Rust↔webview**: TauRPC routers, one router per module crate (`ingest`, `buffer`, `viz`, `ui-bridge`, `snapshot`, `curation`, `triage`, `workspace-detector`, `plugins`, `corpus`, `security`); no manual TypeScript re-declaration of command signatures. Frontend consumes only TauRPC-generated `.ts` bindings.

- **External wire — MCP server**: JSON-RPC 2.0 per MCP spec; tool methods are `query_traces`, `query_metrics`, `query_logs`, `generate_snapshot`, `query_incident_list`, `retrieve_report`, `retrieve_telemetry_slice`, `mark_incident_resolved` (these 4 added chunk #94), `retrieve_incident_events` (added chunk `2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp`). The wire is the console engine's door — line-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 over the Unix-domain socket `run/door/sock`, methods `initialize` · `tools/list` · `tools/call` · `ping` (§Standard Contracts → Engine door; PROVISIONAL — §Occupied Resources → Network ports). That wire is reached over stdio through the relay `andromeda-pulse-engine door`, one connection per request.

Every `tools/list` entry carries a boolean member `write`, true for `mark_incident_resolved` alone (`tools_list_manifest()`, `crates/mcp-server/src/jsonrpc.rs`). The manifest's `additionalProperties: false` is enforced by the door's `declared_only`, the one refusal of an undeclared argument member (`-32602`); the tools' argument structs read past one (read in the source). Capabilities, prompts, resources, sampling sections follow the MCP spec defaults.

- **Engine door — the tools inside the engine's process** (chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process; the form an outside reader depends on — Conductor reads the engine through it): **Connect** — a Unix-domain stream socket at `run/door/sock` under the data dir of a running `andromeda-pulse-engine run`, as the engine's own account. **Admission** — on every accepted connection the peer's account is read from the kernel and must equal the engine's effective account; any other account, root included, and a peer whose account cannot be read, sees the connection closed with no byte written. **Call** — one JSON-RPC 2.0 object per line, UTF-8, at most 65 536 bytes; a request with no `id` is not answered and runs nothing. Methods: `initialize` (`jsonrpc::initialize_result()` unchanged — `serverInfo.name` reads `andromeda-pulse-mcp`, protocol `2024-11-05`) · `tools/list` · `tools/call` · `ping`. `tools/call` carries `params.name` and `params.arguments` and runs one of the nine tools of the entry above through `mcp_server::tools::call_tool` over the engine's own handles — a read connection of the door's own taken from the engine's buffer connection, the engine's `Arc<dyn CorpusWriter>` and its `incident_workspace_key`; the door opens no database and no corpus, reads no `run/workspace-key` and prepares no SQL. `arguments` must be an object whose every member the tool's `inputSchema.properties` declares, else `-32602` before any tool runs. **The one write** — `mark_incident_resolved` answers `-32001` unless `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DOOR_RESOLVE` reads on; `tools/list` names it either way, marked `write`. **Answer** — one line, `result` as the tool returns it, at most 1 048 576 bytes; a longer answer is not cut, the caller gets `-32003`. **Bounds** — a request line over 65 536 bytes: `-32600`, the connection closed · a call over 5 s: `-32002`, and the door interrupts its own read connection · a connection with no complete line for 30 s, or a caller that does not read its answer, is closed · at most 8 connections, a ninth closed at accept · one tool call at a time. **Errors** — the JSON-RPC error object with a fixed message, never the tool's own text: `-32700` parse error · `-32600` request too large · `-32601` unknown tool / method not found · `-32602` invalid arguments · `-32603` tool failed · `-32001` the write is switched off · `-32002` timed out · `-32003` answer too large. So "no such incident" and a fault both read `-32603`. **Records** — `app.boot.door`, `door.call`, `door.refused`, closed labels only (obs-plan §6 and §8 hold their fields). Not shown: that the interrupt ends a real running query (no query of that chunk runs long enough). **Stdio** (since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door) — a caller with no socket client reaches the door by starting `andromeda-pulse-engine door` as the engine's own account. The relay resolves the data dir as `run` does (`engine_boot::resolve_data_dir()`) and canonicalizes the data dir and `{data dir}/run/door/sock` both sides; a socket that does not resolve, resolves outside the data dir, or has a path of 108 bytes or more is unreachable. Each standard-input line that is not whitespace alone takes a connection of its own, in order: the line is sent with its `\n` (an unterminated last line gets one), the write side shut, the whole answer read until the door closes, and only then written to standard output unchanged — the `tools/list` line through the relay equals a direct socket read byte for byte. A line over 65 536 bytes is sent as its first 65 537 bytes with no terminator and the rest of it discarded, never sent. The relay parses nothing, writes no answer of its own, retries nothing and has no time bound of its own; it writes no record and no file. Standard input ending is exit 0; a connect, write, shutdown or read failure on the socket, or a failed write of standard output, is exit 1 with the one fixed standard-error line `andromeda-pulse-engine door: the door cannot be reached` and nothing on standard output from the failed connection; off Unix the word prints that line and exits 1 at once. The door treats the relay as any caller: the account check, one `door.call` per answered request, a request with no `id` answered and recorded with nothing, no idle refusal (one connection per request). Another account through the relay receives no byte: on Linux a refused connection reads `EPIPE` or `ECONNRESET` at the client, so the relay exits 1 with the fixed line (as measured on `ci#38227488889`). The door's own form above is unchanged. Console program only, Unix only, in every build. PROVISIONAL — §Occupied Resources → Network ports, the door.

No DDL change.
  - At-rest posture: cell-level AES-256-GCM encryption is in force; table + column names plaintext, BLOB cell payloads opaque without key (per security-plan.md §Data Protection §At rest; chunk #68 substrate). **Key sourcing is the OS credential store, primary** (macOS Keychain / Linux Secret Service / Windows Credential Manager via the `keyring` crate) — `keyring` 3 is declared with the explicit platform feature set (`apple-native` / `windows-native` / `sync-secret-service` / `crypto-rust`), because keyring 3.x declares NO `default` feature and a bare `keyring = "3"` links no backend at all. The key therefore **persists across processes**: measured at chunk `2026-08-15-corpus-key-persistence` — a second boot decrypted the rows its predecessor wrote with 0 `decryption_failed` (against the 13 that defined the defect), and the Windows entry `corpus-key.com.andromeda.pulse` is present. **Concurrent first creation converges on one key** (chunk `2026-10-04-corpus-key-creation-is-race-free`): `OsKeychainBackend::fetch_from_os_store` is a locked create-or-read — it resolves the per-user lock dir before any keyring call, takes an exclusive `std::fs::File::lock` on the entry's lock file (§Filesystem locations), then gets the entry and, only on `NoEntry`, generates → sets → READS BACK and returns the read-back key, then unlocks; no unlocked generate-and-set path remains. As measured at that chunk: 8 barrier-released re-exec processes against one empty entry ended on 1 distinct key, the one the store held (8 distinct, 7 not stored, on the prior unlocked code). A lock-dir, open or lock failure maps to the existing `KeychainError::Unavailable` / `Failed` and so to `Error::KeyringUnavailable` — it degrades exactly like an unreachable store. **Fallback:** an OPT-IN passphrase supplied via `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_CORPUS_PASSPHRASE`, BLAKE3-derived, nothing written to disk, emitting a once-per-boot WARN announcing reduced key-custody guarantees; it engages only when configured, so a transient store failure can never silently switch keys. On a host with neither a credential store nor a configured passphrase the corpus degrades to absent rather than inventing a key. **Content orphaned by the pre-fix ephemeral-key window is retired at boot** by the inventory-then-purge disposition (`corpus::disposition`) — recovery is cryptographically closed, so the keyless inventory is written before deletion; no DDL and no `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump were needed.

- **One carrier.** A tool call is carried by the door inside the console engine's process (`andromeda-pulse-engine run`; JSON-RPC 2.0, one request per line, over the Unix-domain socket `{data dir}/run/door/sock`; Unix only, the window program seats none): `tools/call` runs `mcp_server::tools::call_tool` over `door::EngineTools`, its one product caller; no `mcp.*` record has an emitter, and no feature or runtime gate exists. The door's one record per call is the log event `door.call` {`method`, `tool`, `outcome`, `write`, `result_type`, `result_count`, `answer_bytes`, `duration_ms`} — once per request that is answered (a request with no `id` is not answered and leaves none), written before the answer line, INFO for `ok` and WARN otherwise, never ERROR; a refused connection or line leaves `door.refused` {`reason`, `peer`} at WARN. The tools' own callee records (`viz.query.traces` / `.metrics` / `.logs`, and for `generate_snapshot` `metric.snapshot.token_count_ms` + `snapshot.token.count.validate`) are written by the console engine on such a call; which of them a real call wrote was not enumerated from a log at that chunk. The door closes an idle connection at 30 s and answers a call over 5 s with `-32002`. Since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door the door carrier is reached two ways: a client of `{data dir}/run/door/sock` directly, or a stdio agent through `andromeda-pulse-engine door` (the relay: one connection per request line, the write side shut after it, the whole answer read and then written to standard output unchanged). Through the relay each answered request leaves one `door.call` in the engine's log, a notification none, and no `door.refused {reason: idle}`; another account's relay reading that reaches the door leaves one `door.refused {other_account, other}` and the relay exits 1 with its fixed standard-error line and 0 bytes on standard output; the relay writes no record itself. **The door is PROVISIONAL — a boundary widening, one item:** the endpoint, the owner check, the reach of the nine tools and of the one write, the write-switch variable and the workflow step that runs a client as a second account are the operator's answers (the pc overseer: at that chunk's P4 dialog, 2026-10-10, and the operator's reading of 2026-10-11 at its wrap); the founder's own word is owed on the surface itself, nothing of it is ratified, and every other statement of the door in this plan rests on this one.

| **P3: MCP server query (JSON-RPC 2.0 tool call)** | IPC-internal + API service + CLI | `duckdb.query.traces` (or metrics/logs per telemetry tool; the five incident tools read the corpus instead), under the door's must-log records `door.call` and `door.refused` — no `mcp.*` span and no gate | `door.call`'s `method`, `tool` (one of the nine `ALL_TOOL_NAMES`: query_traces/metrics/logs/generate_snapshot + query_incident_list/retrieve_report/retrieve_telemetry_slice/mark_incident_resolved/retrieve_incident_events, or `none`), `outcome`, `write`, `result_type`, `result_count`, `answer_bytes`, `duration_ms`; `door.refused`'s `reason`, `peer`; the per-tool reads' `time_range_start`, `time_range_end`, `service_filter` | Tests excerpt P3 ("... asserts `result.traces` is array"); a tool call's one carrier is the console engine's door (a Unix-domain socket, console program only, also reached by a stdio agent through the relay `andromeda-pulse-engine door`, which adds no span, no gate and no record of its own) — §4 Scenario P3, which holds the door's PROVISIONAL sentence |

- **Snapshot / paste-to-AI integration:** Two cleanly separated surfaces.
  - **External-OTLP snapshot** (the product's CORE feature): `snapshot.generate` TauRPC command produces curated markdown from EXTERNAL clients' OTLP data stored in DuckDB ring buffer, saved to `~/.andromeda-pulse/snapshots/{timestamp}.md` per creator brief Section 6 pipeline (time window → filter → curate (dedup, anomaly markers, critical-path extraction, p50/p95/p99 aggregation) → format → token budget enforced ≤ 10k/25k/50k). Four of the nine MCP tools the console engine's door serves (`query_traces`, `query_metrics`, `query_logs`, `generate_snapshot`), over its socket or the `andromeda-pulse-engine door` stdio relay, expose the same pipeline to AI clients; the other five (`query_incident_list`, `retrieve_report`, `retrieve_telemetry_slice`, `mark_incident_resolved`, `retrieve_incident_events`) read the incident corpus. Tool response bodies — all nine — NEVER logged in self-observation file (security plan vector 4); only `result_type` + `result_count` metadata captured.
  - **Self-observation paste-to-AI** (the product's debug surface): the agent reads `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl` directly (JSON-per-line; greppable / jq-able / paste-to-LLM-able). No separate snapshot needed — the JSON log file IS the snapshot. The two surfaces NEVER intersect: external OTLP data lives in DuckDB; self-observation lives in the JSON file.

| **logging-sensitive** | Security plan Section 2 Vector 4: "MCP tool response bodies must NEVER be logged; they surface OTLP attribute values to external LLM clients" | Implement response redaction at the one enforcement site, the console engine's door, which records a tool call as `door.call` with `result_type`, `result_count` and `answer_bytes` — no argument, no answer and no error text, every refusal a fixed message; its negative reading: a marker planted in OTLP content and returned by the owner's `query_logs` stands 0 times in the engine's log family (`pulse-app/tests/integration_door.rs`). |

- `span.kind = "server"` — inbound handlers: `ingest.grpc.export.request` (gRPC), `ingest.http.export.request` (HTTP POST), TauRPC command handlers (the door records a tool call as the log event `door.call` and opens no span)

- **Must-trace spans:** `app.boot` (app entry, parent) → `app.boot.workspace.detect` (startup workspace detection) → `filesystem.scan.gitroot` (find .git/) → `workspace.marker.check` (.andromeda/ present) → `workspace.identity.resolve` (project name resolution)
- **Required log fields:** `trace_id`, `workspace.root_path`, `workspace.project_name`, `vcs_type`, `vcs_root`, `marker_present`, `detection_latency_ms`

| **P7: Workspace detection (.andromeda/ marker)** | desktop-native (app startup) + workspace-detector + IPC-internal | `app.boot.workspace.detect` (startup), `filesystem.scan.gitroot` (find .git/), `workspace.marker.check` (.andromeda/ present), `workspace.identity.resolve` (project name resolution); parent span: `app.boot` | `workspace.root_path`, `workspace.project_name`, `vcs_type` (git), `vcs_root`, `marker_present`, `detection_latency_ms` | Tests excerpt P7 ("Boot app with CWD set to repository root (has `.andromeda/` marker)... invoke TauRPC `workspace.detect()`... assert response.workspace contains project_name, root_path, vcs_type ('git'), vcs_root"); arch excerpt Section 1 Workspace ("workspace-detector — Detect host project context; discovery boundary") |

- **Incident-path diagnostic leaves** (chunk 2026-08-15-tier-1-incident-path-investigation). Each is an EXACT leaf for the same `for_target` prefix-fallback reason, and **no bare `incidents` or `triage` key may exist** — a prefix key would silently widen every sibling target to one field set (asserted by `pulse-app/tests/unit_observability_allowlist_incident_diagnostics.rs`). All three previously resolved to no entry and were redacted in production, which is why locating a downstream zero at the 2026-08-15 arm-zero classification required an out-of-band read-only sqlite3 query of `corpus.db`:
  - `incidents.list_active.request`: `item_count` (count). Live-verified unredacted — the count is observable forming in the log (0 → 1 → 2) on a storm run.
  - `triage.incident.persist`: `incident_count`, `persist_kind`, `duration_ms`, `declined_count`, `reconciled_count`. **All FIVE fields, not two and no longer three or four** — the emit site (`crates/triage/src/incident/persistence.rs::run_incident_persist_cycle`) is the authority, and a leaf naming fewer leaves the target PARTLY redacted (the shape no resolver probe can see, because the named fields keep rendering fine). `duration_ms` was the field the original two-field entry missed; `declined_count` joined at chunk `2026-08-27-incident-persist-vs-resolve-write-race`, counting stale writes the corpus monotonic guard DECLINED; `reconciled_count` joined at chunk `2026-08-29-app-registry-reconciliation`, counting registry rows dropped because the persistent corpus already held them resolved — written by `mark_incident_resolved` through the console engine's door, the running engine dropping such a row from its active set within one persist cycle — each folded ONCE per persist cycle onto this existing record, never per row, never per declined write and never per reconciled row, per the §11 hot-path ban (the cycle walks every active row). The pair is also the leg's discriminator: `reconciled_count` 1 / `declined_count` 0 post-fix against 0 / 2 under a mutation with reconciliation removed. They are aggregate counts only: never incident identity, `scope_id`, workspace, title/detail, payload, the UPDATE's SQL text, or its bound parameter values. `persist_kind` is typed `&'static str` at the emit site, so its domain is bounded by construction. The guard asserts the field set by EQUALITY in both directions (`pulse-app/tests/unit_observability_allowlist_incident_diagnostics.rs`), which is what catches a narrowed leaf; live-verified unredacted at the chunk's GREEN leg on 13 persist records.
  - `triage.incident.corpus_restore`: `kind`, `restored_incident_count` — literal label + count; never incident identity or workspace.

| `warn` | Recoverable errors + degraded performance + retry-able | `warn!(target: "config.load.path_validation", "path canonicalization rejected")` on CWE-22 violation; `warn!(target: "app.boot.buffer.degraded", reason, consequence)` — fires ONCE per boot when the buffer connection is absent, because the fallback drains and discards ingest batches while ingest's own counters keep climbing, making a degraded boot otherwise indistinguishable from a healthy one; `warn!(target: "corpus.keychain.fallback", backend_kind, reason, consequence)` — ONCE per boot when the passphrase branch serves the corpus key instead of the OS credential store, for the same reason (a reduced-custody boot is otherwise indistinguishable from a keychain-primary one); `warn!(target: "corpus.orphan.disposition", disposition_outcome, rows_purged, tables_affected)` — once per boot pass, aggregate counts only; `warn!(target: "corpus.read.undecryptable", query_id, rows_skipped)` — ONE aggregate per QUERY, never per row (§11 hot-path spam ban), so a corpus holding undecryptable rows degrades visibly instead of going dark; `warn!(target: "triage.baseline.bootstrap_window.override", resolved_seconds, default_seconds, reason)` — ONCE per boot and only when the resolved cold-start window differs from the 3600s default, because an env-shortened (or env-rejected) bound silently changes when every service becomes eligible for silence detection, making such a boot otherwise indistinguishable from a default one; `warn!(target: "buffer.consumer.stalled", reason, consequence, stalled_seconds, buffer_capacity_pct)` — emitted by the drain-progress classifier ONCE per healthy→stalled transition and once again on recovery, never per batch, because a wedged consumer keeps emitting `buffer.tick` and is otherwise indistinguishable from a healthy one (measured 2026-08-26: `rows_ingested` frozen 16 minutes, 0 ERROR, all ticks normal); fires only after 30 consecutive non-draining ticks (450s), deliberately above §10's 420s sustained-drain cap so an in-spec drain cannot trip it (chunk 2026-08-26-ingest-consumer-stall-under-sustained-load); `warn!(target: "app.boot.window.navigation", window_label, navigated, reason)` — at most ONCE PER WINDOW PER BOOT (bounded by the 4-entry declared-window set), fired post-settle and off any hot path, INFO when the window navigated and WARN when it is still on `about:blank`, because a webview that loses its initial navigation is never re-navigated (`show()` is not navigation) and surfaces as a blank window on first open, which no other signal distinguishes from a healthy boot (chunk 2026-08-24-headful-mechanics-probe-race-disposition); `warn!(target: "app.exit", exit_class, exit_code, exit_code_known, signal)` — EXACTLY ONCE per process end (a process-wide once-flag, first emitter wins; the emitter then drops the only `WorkerGuard`, so no second record can reach the file), off any hot path per §11: WARN for `signal` (SIGTERM/SIGINT on Unix, recorded from a runtime task, then the same signal re-raised with the default disposition so the process still ends BY it), ERROR for a non-zero `event_loop` exit and every `outside_event_loop` end (the `atexit` hook, which hands off to a `pulse-exit-reporter` thread and waits ≤ 2 s — `exit_code` 0 with `exit_code_known: false`, because `libc` binds no `on_exit`), INFO for a zero-code `event_loop` exit (Tray Quit), because a process end otherwise leaves no record at all — the 69f0b93 Linux CI boot smoke ended `exit 1` with 0 `app.panic.fatal` and no cause; the loggable and unloggable ends are listed in §7 (chunk 2026-10-01-conductor-return); `warn!(target: "app.boot.render.posture", posture, lever)` — EXACTLY ONCE per window-app boot (the console program emits none, asserted on a spawned run), emitted by `main` after `engine_boot::init_process` has initialised the sink (the decision is taken at the head of `main()`, where no subscriber exists, and carried as a value), off any hot path per §11: WARN for `preset_honoured` (a launch-env value of `__NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC` was honoured — an overridden posture), INFO for `applied` (the Linux default `1` was set) and `not_applicable` (macOS / Windows), because a preset-honoured boot is otherwise indistinguishable from a default-applied one; `lever` carries the variable NAME only, never its value (chunk 2026-10-04-linux-launch-stays-up-on-nvidia-wayland); `warn!(target: "app.boot.engine", program, interpretation, reason)` — EXACTLY ONCE per `engine_boot::start`, so once per boot of either program, off any hot path per §11: WARN when `interpretation` is `none` (the console program with `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC` unset seats no runner — cues and digests are produced and no incident forms), INFO for `model` and `deterministic`; the one record that names which program booted and what sits in the interpretation seat, all three fields closed labels (§8; chunk 2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point); `warn!(target: "app.boot.door", state, resolve_write)` — once per boot of a program that seats the door (the console program on Unix; the window app writes none), off any hot path per §11: INFO when `state` is `listening` and the switch is not `rejected`, WARN otherwise (`path_too_long` | `in_use` | `occupied` | `bind_failed`, in each of which the engine goes on with no door; or `resolve_write` `rejected`); `warn!(target: "door.call", method, tool, outcome, write, result_type, result_count, answer_bytes, duration_ms)` — once per request that is answered, written before the answer line, INFO for `ok` and WARN for the other eight outcomes; `warn!(target: "door.refused", reason, peer)` — WARN, one per refused connection or line (`other_account` | `too_many_connections` | `request_too_large` | `idle`); none of the three is ever written at ERROR (§8; chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process; PROVISIONAL — §4 Scenario P3); `warn!(target: "interpretation.model.allow_root", confinement, root_basename)` — EXACTLY ONCE per window-app boot (the console program reads no `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_ALLOW_ROOT`, constructs no `LlamaCliInference` and writes no `interpretation.model.*` record), WARN when `confinement = "unconfined"` (no `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_ALLOW_ROOT` set, so the L4 model/binary paths resolve unconfined) or `"unresolvable"` (set but not a directory ⇒ fail-closed, every candidate rejected), and INFO when `"enforced"` — because an unconfined L4 boot is otherwise indistinguishable from a confined one, which is precisely what made the prior posture a silent convention; `warn!(target: "interpretation.model.load.error", env_var, error_category, path_basename, recovery_action)` — per REJECTED candidate, bounded to the two path reads at `LlamaCliInference::new` and therefore off any hot path per §11, with `error_category` drawn from the bounded set `traversal_component` | `path_too_long` | `canonicalize_failed` | `not_regular_file` | `outside_allow_root` | `allow_root_unresolvable` (chunk 2026-08-26-l4-runtime-security-residuals); `warn!(target: "ui.ipc.rejection", error_category, window_label, payload_bytes)` — ONCE per capability-rejected webview IPC (never per invoke; off any hot path per §11), reported from the webview catch through `telemetry.frontend.record_ipc_rejection` with `error_category` bounded by a closed serde enum (`acl_rejected` | `other`, classified webview-side from the rejection value), because a capability-rejected IPC otherwise leaves no record at all and a revoked grant is indistinguishable from a working affordance (measured: granted world 0×, revoked world exactly one record while `copy_state: "error"` kept the UX byte-identical — chunk 2026-08-30-acl-rejection-logging); `warn!(target: "ui.webgpu.adapter", outcome, window_label)` — ONCE per canvas-mount WebGPU adapter request (once per `requestWebGPUAdapter()` return path, never per frame; off any hot path per §11), reported fire-and-forget from `canvas/adapter-state.ts::reportAdapterOutcome` through `telemetry.frontend.record_webgpu_adapter` (the 6th `telemetry.frontend.*` method — the founder's ratification at P4 2026-09-30: «Да, делай»), INFO on `obtained` and WARN on `no_navigator_gpu` | `adapter_null` | `adapter_request_rejected` | `device_request_failed` (a closed serde enum; an unknown value is rejected), so a 0-frame run can name its cause from its own log (§10 frame row; chunk 2026-09-30-perf-instruments-measure-their-budgets) |

| `mcp-server` (the tools library the door serves) | none of its own — a tool call is logged by the door as `door.call` (`info` for `ok`, `warn` otherwise) | The library writes no `mcp.*` record; the console engine's door logs each answered call |

- **Logging stack:** `tracing` 0.1 + `tracing-subscriber` 0.3 JSON formatter + `tracing-appender` 0.2 daily-rolling file sink + `tracing-error` 0.2 SpanTrace for sanitized error chains. The app has a SINGLE sink: the file `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl`, always JSON-only — no stderr `tracing` layer, no TTY pretty-print (as measured at chunk `2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp`: `observability::init` builds the file layer only). The console program's `door` word (the stdio relay) writes no `tracing` output at all; its stdout is reserved for the door's answer lines.

- NEVER write to the stdout of the console program's `door` word (the stdio relay) anything but the door's answer bytes, unchanged, or to its stderr anything but the one fixed line on exit 1 — its stdout carries the door's JSON-RPC 2.0 answers, and ANY accidental `println!` / `dbg!` / library stdout write corrupts them for the agent; it installs no `tracing` subscriber and writes no record (PROVISIONAL with the door's item)

| `xtask test` (the `lint-test` job) | the tests' own output; the job boots no window app and no step of it writes a log family under an uploaded path (as measured on `ci#38031822696`); six test binaries of the run start the console program (`andromeda-pulse-engine run`) — `integration_console_engine` since chunk 2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point, since chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed the two `xtask/tests` binaries `agent_run_shell` and `engine_cycle_refusals`, through the committed `scripts/agent-run.sh` and the built `harness:engine-cycle` verb, `integration_door`, and the two door-reading tests `e2e_p3_mcp_subprocess_tools_call` and `security_mcp_response_body_redaction` — the first four each under a cleared environment with no display variable and no session bus, and each engine writes its log family under the data dir its test gives it, which no step uploads | none uploaded from the test run; the perf-samples producer that follows it in the job writes the log `perf:budget` grades, uploaded as `logs-perf-samples-Linux` |

- **Sink:** Single sink for app: the file `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl`, always JSON-only, via the non-blocking `tracing-appender` daily layer composed with `EnvFilter` + `ErrorLayer` — no stderr layer, no TTY pretty-print (as measured at chunk `2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp`). The console program's `door` word (the stdio relay, chunk `2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door`; PROVISIONAL with the door's item) has no sink at all — no subscriber, no record — its stdout reserved for the door's JSON-RPC answer lines and its stderr for one fixed line on exit 1
- **service.name:** compile-time constant `"com.andromeda.pulse"` (Tauri bundle identifier; fallback `env!("CARGO_PKG_NAME")` = "pulse-app")

- **MCP tools (hand-rolled JSON-RPC 2.0 through the door):** nine (`ALL_TOOL_NAMES`) — `query_traces`, `query_metrics`, `query_logs`, `generate_snapshot` are the JSON-RPC 2.0 interface to the same external-OTLP query pipeline; `query_incident_list`, `retrieve_report`, `retrieve_telemetry_slice`, `mark_incident_resolved` (chunk #94) and `retrieve_incident_events` (chunk `2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp`) read the incident corpus. The console engine's door serves every tool through `mcp_server::tools::call_tool` (it returns `ToolAnswer { value, result_type, result_count }` and writes no record), its one product caller `door::EngineTools`; each call is recorded as `door.call` carrying `result_type` + `result_count` and never the answer (result metadata only, NOT result_content per security plan vector 4). Over stdio means the `andromeda-pulse-engine door` relay alone, which carries each line to the door's Unix-domain socket; calls through it are recorded as `door.call` only (obs-plan §4 Scenario P3). The `duckdb.query.{traces|metrics|logs}` child belongs to the telemetry tools only

body:
- **Vector:** the console engine's door (a Unix-domain socket; chunk `2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process`)
  - **Entry point:** the Unix-domain stream socket `{data dir}/run/door/sock` (mode 0600, inside `run/door/`, mode 0700), opened by `andromeda-pulse-engine run` alone — the window app opens none, and off Unix none is seated. JSON-RPC 2.0, one request per line: `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `ping`. `tools/call` serves the nine tools in the engine's own process, over the engine's buffer read connection, its `CorpusWriter` and its `incident_workspace_key`. One write, `mark_incident_resolved`, behind the `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DOOR_RESOLVE` switch. Conductor is the named reader. Since chunk `2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door` a stdio agent reaches the door through `andromeda-pulse-engine door`, a short-lived relay it starts (one per agent session) — a client of `run/door/sock`, one connection per request line, with no listener, port, file, pid file, variable or log record of its own; the door treats it as any caller (the account check; one `door.call` per answered request; a request with no `id` answered and recorded with nothing; no idle refusal). It is a way through the door, not a second way in: the engine has one way in besides telemetry, this door, reached over its socket or through the stdio relay.
  - **Trust boundary:** own host only — no TCP port and no network listener is added. The caller must be the engine's own account by the kernel's peer credential (§Authentication & Authorization): any other account, root included, is closed with no byte written. The directory's and the socket's modes are outer layers that hold an unprivileged account and do not hold root. Requests are bounded and refused with fixed messages (§Input Validation). **PROVISIONAL — a boundary widening, one item:** the endpoint, the owner check, the reach of the nine tools and of the one write, the write-switch variable and the workflow step that runs a client as a second account are the operator's answers (the pc overseer: at that chunk's P4 dialog, 2026-10-10, and the operator's reading of 2026-10-11 at its wrap); the founder's own word is owed on the surface itself, and nothing of it is ratified. Since chunk `2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door` the same item also covers the console program's third word `door` (the stdio relay) and the step's second arm: the operator's answers at that chunk's P4 (the pc overseer, 2026-10-12) and at its operator pass, and the operator's answer as the founder's delegate at its wrap; the founder's own word is still owed. Every other statement of the door in this plan rests on this one.

- **Networking:** local only — OTLP receivers bound `127.0.0.1` only; since chunk `2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process` the console engine also serves the nine tools over a Unix-domain socket inside the data dir (`run/door/sock`) — own host only, no TCP or network listener added; updater is outbound HTTPS to GitHub Releases; no inbound internet exposure.

**Boundary:** validate at ALL system boundaries — wherever untrusted data
enters the system. The dominant boundaries here are the loopback OTLP receivers, the TauRPC bridge, the WASM plugin host, the console engine's door socket (since chunk `2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process`), the console program's command line, and env-var/config-file inputs.

| MCP tool inputs (`mcp-server` crate, served through the console engine's door alone — all 9 tools dispatched by name: `query_traces`/`query_metrics`/`query_logs`/`generate_snapshot` + the chunk #94 corpus-backed `query_incident_list`/`retrieve_report`/`retrieve_telemetry_slice`/`mark_incident_resolved` + the chunk `2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp` `retrieve_incident_events`, whose `{incident_id: integer}` input deserializes through the serde `IncidentIdArgs` with `additionalProperties: false` and whose corpus read is a prepared `?1`/`?2` statement bounded at `INCIDENT_EVENTS_READ_LIMIT` = 256, never selecting `payload`) | Hand-rolled serde JSON-RPC 2.0 framing (`crates/mcp-server/src/jsonrpc.rs`, MCP protocol `2024-11-05`, name-dispatch via `mcp_server::tools::call_tool`, whose one product caller is `door::EngineTools`; no `rmcp`); tool argument structs via `serde`; query parameters routed through the same DuckDB prepared-statement boundary above | No `rmcp`: it is in no manifest and not in `Cargo.lock`. Tool argument structs use `serde`; the `query_*` tools share the `viz` crate's prepared-statement code path. Snapshot tool output is not sanitized for LLM-side prompt injection — see §Code Patterns anti-patterns and §Logging redaction notes. **An undeclared argument member:** the tool manifest declares `additionalProperties: false` on every tool, and the door's `declared_only` is the one refusal of it — `-32602` for all nine tools before any tool runs, nothing of it answered (the next row; PROVISIONAL — §Threat Model Summary → Attack surface, the door's vector); the argument structs (`QueryTracesArgs`, `QueryMetricsArgs`, `QueryLogsArgs`, `GenerateSnapshotArgs`, `IncidentIdArgs`) carry no `deny_unknown_fields`. `call_tool` returns `ToolAnswer` and writes no log record; `tools/list` gives every tool a boolean `write`, true for `mark_incident_resolved` alone. |

- MCP `query_*` and `generate_snapshot` tool responses are the indirect-prompt-injection surface that the calling LLM client must defend itself against per security-research §rmcp; the receiver app cannot fully sanitize OTLP-derived attribute values. This is intended behavior, not a defect; the guidance a reader needs ("Using MCP with andromeda-pulse") is not written — no such document is in the tree (research's `git grep -l -i 'Using MCP with andromeda-pulse'` at chunk `2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door` hit only 2026-05-02 security run files) — and is owned by the route entry `Records say what the product is`.
```
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo xtask capability-widening-check
cargo xtask check:ingest-progress
cargo xtask check:staged-artifacts        # staged bindings + capability grants vs pins (exit 0/1/2; also runs inside capability-drift)
cargo xtask capability-drift              # BEFORE the workspace nextest — see the ordering note below
cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci
cargo nextest run -p pulse-app --bin pulse-app -E 'test(emit_taurpc_bindings)'   # bindings regen: the last cargo-adjacent step
git diff --quiet <chunk-base> -- pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts   # the close, for a chunk adding no procedure
npm run lint --prefix pulse-app/ui        # webview gates: only when pulse-app/ui/** touched
npm run typecheck --prefix pulse-app/ui
npm run test --prefix pulse-app/ui
```

`cargo xtask capability-drift` runs BEFORE the default-features `cargo nextest run --workspace` (the overseer's founder-delegated directive of 2026-09-30, first run at chunk 2026-09-30-dual-license). That workspace run rewrites `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` (`taurpc`'s `export_types()` on every `Router::into_handler()`) in the default build's shape, which is the whole procedure set, so it does not shrink the bindings; the drift read runs before it all the same. The `emit_taurpc_bindings` regen, with no feature, then follows the workspace run as the LAST cargo-adjacent step, and a probe named against the chunk base closes the sequence: `git diff --quiet <chunk-base> -- pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts`, exit 0 meaning the bindings end byte-identical to the base. That close is what was measured, for a chunk that adds no TauRPC procedure. A chunk that CHANGES the procedure set closes instead with (first run at chunk 2026-09-30-perf-instruments-measure-their-budgets, approved by the operator at its wrap): the regen after the workspace run → a content probe on the worktree bindings (the new procedure's name) → `git add` of the regenerated bindings WITH the `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` pin (index only, no commit) → `check:staged-artifacts`, then `capability-drift` LAST — both read the staged copy, and before the regen the committed bindings lack the pinned procedure, so drift cannot run earlier. The regen must also PRECEDE the `ui/dist` build and every release build a live leg drives: the taurpc proxy resolves methods against the `ARGS_MAP` bundled into `ui/dist`, so a dist built before the regen ships without the new method and a fire-and-forget caller no-ops silently (measured at that chunk: 1 bundle occurrence — the caller's own property access — vs 2 once rebuilt after the regen). `cargo xtask check:staged-artifacts` (added 2026-08-30-staged-bindings-assertion, `xtask/src/staged_gate.rs`) makes the staged assertion CODE inside the gate itself: it reads the git-INDEX copies of `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` + all `pulse-app/capabilities/*.json` (via a `git ls-files --stage` health probe then `git show :<path>` per subject) against `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` + `staged_gate::EXPECTED_GRANTS`, with one pretty-JSON verdict on stdout (`{gate:"staged-artifacts", arm, verdict, bindings{…}, grants{…}}`), arms `staged-clean`/`staged-drift`/`cannot-evaluate` at exit 0/1/2, report twin `target/staged-artifacts/report.json`, and a staged DELETION of a subject or an UNPINNED `pulse-app/capabilities/*.json` file findings-RED (no neutral arm) — and `capability_drift()` RUNS that same staged assertion after its unchanged worktree diff, folding ANY non-clean staged outcome into its existing 0/1 failure exit. The worktree can be correct while the index carries a clobbered version — exactly what the staged read catches (playbook.md 2026-08-22's ORDERING rule stands; its interim manual `git show | grep` assertion is superseded by the shipped gate).

`cargo xtask smoke:external-resolve` (added 2026-08-29, chunk `2026-08-29-app-registry-reconciliation`) is the **second SCENARIO leg** in that family — likewise **NOT a member of the standard gate set**, dev-host only, not CI-wired, `xtask/src/external_resolve.rs` with `--bootstrap-seconds` / `--observe-seconds`. It refuses at its precondition: the `andromeda-pulse-mcp` binary it resolves through is built by no target, its leg against the console engine owned by the route entry «Scenario legs driven against the console engine» (CARRY 2). It runs the direct-binary smoke form (fresh `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` + `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_BASELINE_BOOTSTRAP_SECONDS` + `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC` set into the spawned app) and drives the app-registry-vs-durable-store divergence end to end: boot → finite storm over real OTLP → resolve an incident through a REAL `andromeda-pulse-mcp` subprocess → observe two 60 s persist cycles. **The verdict keys on `reconciled_count` (≥ 1) and `declined_count` (0) — explicitly NOT on `item_count`, which is printed as context only.** That exclusion is measured, not stylistic: under a mutation removing reconciliation, `item_count` still went 2 → 0 in BOTH arms, because the finite storm's auto-resolve fires 120 s after the last re-emission and the observation window covers it — a verdict keyed on the drop would have passed in both worlds. GREEN measured `reconciled 1 / declined 0`; the mutation arm measured `reconciled 0 / declined 2`, the pre-fix signature. **Two shaping constraints, both measured:** `--sustained` CANNOT drive this leg (it holds a constant error rate, so the cue evaluator's short/long EWMA ratio converges and never trips the gate — 0 incidents in 240 s), and the finite injector must be BACKGROUNDED rather than awaited, or the 120 s auto-resolve window closes before the external write lands and the sidecar has nothing active to resolve. Like its sibling it **proves its own preconditions** — no incident visible to the sidecar, or a resolve the guard did not apply, reports INCONCLUSIVE rather than PASS — and it refuses an `--observe-seconds` below two persist cycles up front (`observe_window_supports_verdict`), the same structurally-impossible-verdict guard `smoke:gap-resume` carries.

- Actions:

## 2026-11-03-stdio-sidecar-retired — tool responses through the door alone, and the records the sidecar wrote
**Section:** §Logging & Monitoring (the prompt-injection hygiene note; What NEVER to log, the door's bullet); §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging (the `incident_events` NO-SCRUB paragraph; the lock-dir clause of the full-path ban)
**Change:**
- The hygiene note had a second carrier (the door) and a third (the relay), the note applying "as to the sidecar's client". Now tool responses reach an agent through the console engine's door alone: over its socket, or written byte for byte to standard output by `andromeda-pulse-engine door`. The note applies to an agent reading through either (PROVISIONAL, the door's vector).
- The door's NEVER-log bullet was "a tool response body on a second carrier"; it now reads "a tool response body".
- `incident_events`: the vocabulary was read by the sidecar and is now read by the `retrieve_incident_events` tool. `mark_incident_resolved` reaches `update_incident_status` through the door alone (was the cross-process sidecar and the door). The one reader is served by the door alone through `call_tool` (was the sidecar and the door). The canary absence was measured on stderr and the file sink; it now reads the file sink.
- Lock-failure records were `corpus.open.error` / `mcp.boot.corpus.init`; they are now `corpus.open.error` alone.
**Why:** the chunk retires the sidecar, its stderr-JSON sink and the `mcp.*` record chain. No `mcp.*` record has an emitter in product code any more, and `call_tool`'s one product caller is the door.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-03T04-03-49Z-wrap/

## 2026-11-03-stdio-sidecar-retired — the stdio sidecar retired; mcp-server the tools library the door serves
**Section:** §1 Test Scope Summary (the Justification; Coverage scope: the mcp-server row, the console engine program row; Surfaces under test: the MCP stdio sidecar row); §4 Unit Test Strategy (the mcp-server crate); §5 Integration Test Strategy (the module driver); §6 E2E Test Strategy (the driver row); §8 Mocking & Stubbing Discipline (the process row)
**Change:**
- The Justification's entity list names the mcp-server tools served through the console engine door (was the MCP sidecar).
- The mcp-server row reads "the tools library the door serves": no binary, no cargo feature and no env gate; the crate holds `contract`, `jsonrpc` and `tools`, and `pulse-app` names it as a plain dependency; `mcp_server::tools::call_tool` has one product caller, `door::EngineTools::call` (was a feature-gated, runtime-gated stdio sidecar with `rmcp` a feature-gated anchor dependency and `dispatch_tool` calling `call_tool`); `tools_list_manifest()` still marks `mark_incident_resolved` alone as a write.
- The console engine program is one of the two product binaries, beside `pulse-app` (was the third, beside `pulse-app` and `andromeda-pulse-mcp`).
- The MCP stdio sidecar surface row reads N/A — retired: no sidecar binary, no compile-time or runtime gate, no subprocess test; a stdio agent reaches the nine tools through the relay `andromeda-pulse-engine door`.
- §4: the mcp-server crate's unit scope names tool call routing (`call_tool`) and drops feature-gate build verification.
- §5: Module ↔ engine door, a `tokio::net::UnixStream` client writing JSON-RPC 2.0 lines to `run/door/sock` on an engine booted by `engine_boot::start` or a spawned `andromeda-pulse-engine run` (was Module ↔ MCP sidecar over `tokio::process::Command`).
- §6: the console engine door row replaces the MCP stdio sidecar row: no feature flag, no env var, one request per line, the answer line parsed.
- §8: the process row spawns the built `andromeda-pulse-engine` (`run`, or the `door` relay), no mocking library (was `tokio::process::Command` on the sidecar).
**Why:** the chunk removed the `andromeda-pulse-mcp` binary, its double gate (`--features mcp-server` + `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED`), `rmcp`, `feature_gate`, `tracing_setup`, `dispatch_tool` and the sidecar's subprocess tests; `mcp-server` stays a workspace member as the tools library the door serves.

## 2026-11-03-stdio-sidecar-retired — P3 driven through the console engine door
**Section:** §1 Test Scope Summary (Critical paths: P3); Scenario: P3 — MCP server query (Surfaces involved, Steps, Cleanup)
**Change:**
- P3: the agent spawns `andromeda-pulse-engine run`, sends telemetry over OTLP, writes a JSON-RPC 2.0 `tools/call` line to the door (`run/door/sock`, or the stdio relay `andromeda-pulse-engine door`), asserts `result` and the tool's shape and one `door.call` record per answered request (`pulse-app/tests/e2e_p3_mcp_subprocess_tools_call.rs`); no feature flag, no env gate (was the feature-gated sidecar fed on stdin).
- Surfaces involved: the console engine door, socket or stdio relay (was the MCP stdio sidecar, feature-gated).
- Steps: spawn the engine on its own data dir and two claimed loopback ports; send spans and logs over OTLP gRPC; ask through `run/door/sock`, one connection per request line; `tools/call` lines for `query_traces`, `query_metrics`, `query_logs`, `generate_snapshot` and two carrying an SQL-injection fragment and a sentinel cursor; the four calls answer `result`; each tool's shape, one `door.call` per answered request, the fragment and the sentinel 0 times in the log family (was a feature build, a sidecar spawn and `result.traces` read on stdout).
- Cleanup: end the spawned engine by SIGTERM and read its log family after the end (was SIGTERM to the sidecar PID, exit 0, no zombie).
**Why:** the sidecar left; the P3 test reads through the door of a spawned engine, and the SQL-injection and response-sentinel canaries became one door arm, `p3_mcp_tools_call_sql_injection_and_sentinel_cursor_stay_out_of_the_log`.
